meta.chainStory: Hotel Trame (Rome, independent) → W Florence (Marriott Luxury) → Il Castelfalfi (Tuscany, TUI Blue Selection) → Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria (Sorrento, Leading Hotels of the World) → InterContinental Rome Ambasciatori Palace (IHG)

days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Jet-lag day. Nothing ticketed, nothing timed — the only fixed point is dinner.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Private driver to Hotel Trame
items.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board. Licensed cars may enter the ZTL to set down, so you are dropped at the hotel door — no garage, no walk with the bags.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: A former Franciscan monastery a few streets off Campo de' Fiori

items.title: First walk: Pantheon → Piazza Navona → Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The Pantheon is an eight-minute walk. Go before the nap, not after.

items.title: Nap, deliberately
items.detail: Set an alarm. This is the single best defence against day-two jet lag.

items.title: Aperitivo at Etabli
items.detail: Or the Campari bar on Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Dinner — Armando al Pantheon
items.detail: Tiny, family-run, and booked out weeks ahead. Reserve now.

days.title: The Vatican, before anyone else
days.note: Early entry is the whole point: the Sistine Chapel is a different room with 40 people in it than with 400.

items.title: Vatican early-entry private tour
items.detail: Into the Sistine Chapel before general admission

items.title: Lunch — Da Romolo or Hostaria Dino e Tony
items.detail: Unfussy Roman cooking a short walk from the museum exit

items.title: Back to the hotel through the heat
items.detail: Late August in Rome peaks around 3pm. Don't fight it.

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then the bridge at sunset
items.detail: Ponte Sant'Angelo with Bernini's angels catching the last light

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Confirm the Aug 25 programme; Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci; a properly Roman hour to eat

days.title: Ancient Rome, end to end
days.note: Last full Roman day before Florence — this afternoon is also the Villa Borghese photo session, so the siesta runs shorter than usual.

items.title: Colosseum with arena floor, then Forum + Palatine
items.detail: The arena-floor add-on is worth it — you stand where the sand was

items.title: Lunch — Roscioli
items.detail: Carbonara and cacio e pepe, and the deli counter on the way out
items.how: Walk, 5 min via Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Siesta
items.detail: Shorter than the other days — the light at Borghese is worth trading a bit of rest for

items.title: Villa Borghese Gardens, in the daylight
items.detail: Rome's largest park — shaded avenues, the Fontana dei Cavalli Marini, and the Pincio terrace over Piazza del Popolo with St. Peter's dome on the skyline. Soft light under the trees most of the afternoon — good ground for pictures. The Galleria itself needs a timed ticket booked weeks out; skip it unless you already have one.

items.title: Down to Piazza del Popolo
items.detail: The twin churches and the obelisk, down the Pincio steps

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: North to Florence, and straight into it
days.changeNote: Florence now comes second, right after Rome — the W sits on Piazza dell'Unità Italiana, two minutes from the platform, so the travel day costs you almost no sightseeing time.

items.title: Check out; taxi to Roma Termini
items.detail: About fifteen minutes from Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Frecciarossa to Florence
items.detail: Roma Termini → Firenze S.M.N., direct — about 1h30. Departures roughly every half hour; book ahead for the fare, not for the seat.

items.title: Drop bags — W Florence
items.detail: Piazza dell'Unità Italiana, a two-minute walk from the station door. Rooms are ready from 3:00pm; they'll hold the luggage.

items.title: Lunch — Trattoria Mario, by San Lorenzo
items.detail: Shared tables, cash, closed by 3:30pm. Mercato Centrale upstairs is the no-queue fallback.

items.title: Accademia — David at the afternoon slot
items.detail: Forty-five minutes is genuinely enough. Go straight down the hall of the Prisoners.

items.title: The Duomo complex — Baptistery, cathedral, museum
items.detail: Everything but the dome climb, which is booked for tomorrow's first slot. The Ghiberti doors in the Opera del Duomo museum are the originals.

items.title: Piazza della Signoria and the Loggia dei Lanzi
items.detail: An open-air sculpture hall, and it is free

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is around 8:00pm. Taxi up, walk down through the rose garden.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a handful of window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: The dome, the Uffizi, and the far side of the river
days.note: Dense by design, and the only complete Florence day you get. Everything before noon is ticketed and time-stamped; everything after is yours.

items.title: Duomo — climb Brunelleschi's dome
items.detail: 463 steps, timed slot, and far better before the day heats up. Book this one first — it has the fewest slots of anything in the city.

items.title: Coffee on the way down to the river
Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. Roughly two hours with a guide, which is the right amount.

items.title: Lunch in the Oltrarno — Il Santo Bevitore
items.detail: Or Gucci Osteria on Piazza della Signoria if you want the splurge instead.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: The gardens are the reason to go; climb to the top for the view back over the city

items.title: Oltrarno artisan workshops
items.detail: Via Maggio and Santo Spirito — gilders, leatherworkers and restorers still working at street level

items.title: Back to the hotel to change
OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita. A chamber staging in a small church — closer to the singers than any opera house puts you.

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: Into the Val d'Elsa, through Certaldo
days.changeNote: The rental car is collected here and returned in Florence on Aug 31 — two days of driving in the whole trip, and none of it in a city centre.

items.title: Check out; collect the rental car
items.detail: The agencies cluster on Borgo Ognissanti, about eight minutes on foot from the W and just outside the ZTL — so you never drive into the centro storico. Have the IDP and licence ready.

items.title: Southwest out of the city
items.detail: Florence → Certaldo is about 45 minutes

items.title: Certaldo Alto, by funicular
items.detail: Boccaccio's birthplace — a walled brick town, the funicular climbs from Piazza Boccaccio in under two minutes

items.title: Casa Boccaccio
items.detail: The Decameron's author was born here; the house is now a small, quiet museum

items.title: Lunch on Via Boccaccio
items.detail: A terrace table in the upper town before the drive on

items.title: On to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes further into the Val d'Elsa

items.title: Check in — Il Castelfalfi
items.detail: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, its own castle at the centre

items.title: The hamlet on foot
items.detail: The piazza, the castle walls, the little church — all restored, none of it roped off

items.title: Aperitivo at Ecrù
items.detail: The estate's cocktail bar

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room; the vegetables and olive oil are grown on the property

days.title: Towers, then on horseback through the vines
days.kicker: TUSCANY — San Gimignano and a horseback vineyard tour
days.note: One day for both San Gimignano and the horseback vineyard tour — Tuscany is two nights, so Volterra and a separate wine estate don't fit this time.

items.title: Drive to San Gimignano
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: The towers of San Gimignano
items.detail: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval towers still stand — best seen from Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: The Collegiata
items.detail: Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli frescoes wall to wall in a church the size of a chapel

items.title: Gelato at Dondoli
items.detail: A two-time world gelato champion on Piazza della Cisterna — quick, before the horses

items.title: Horseback riding, lunch and a winery
items.detail: San Gimignano Experience: about an hour in the saddle through vineyards, olive groves and native woods, then a traditional Tuscan lunch (antipasti, truffle lasagna, bread soup), a cellar tour and tastings of Chianti Classico, Vernaccia and Super Tuscans. No riding experience needed; book ahead — 3-4 hours all told.
items.how: Meet at the Bivio Volterra bus stop

items.title: Back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: Pool or spa terrace
items.detail: You've earned it after a day in the saddle

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room, on your last Tuscan night

days.title: The long haul south, to one bed for five nights
days.kicker: TUSCANY → SORRENTO — car back to Florence, rail to Naples, driver over the peninsula
days.changeNote: The longest travel day of the trip, and the last one — everything after this is a day trip from a single base. One of you is working remotely from Aug 31 to Sep 5, so the coast is now one hotel rather than three.
days.note: Start early; this is three legs back to back. The Circumvesuviana train from Naples to Sorrento is cheap but has no luggage space in August — take the pre-booked car.

items.title: Check out; on the road
items.detail: Back toward Florence, retracing Saturday's route

items.title: Drop off the rental car
items.detail: Borgo Ognissanti — the two-day rental ends where it started

items.title: Frecciarossa to Naples
items.detail: Firenze S.M.N. → Napoli Centrale, direct via Rome — about 3 hours. Book this one ahead; it's the leg where a good fare is worth having.

items.title: Arrive Napoli Centrale
items.detail: Pre-booked driver meets you on the concourse

items.title: Driver around the bay to Sorrento
items.detail: About 1h15 past Vesuvius and along the peninsula — the coast road tightens the whole way

items.title: Check in — Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria
items.detail: Piazza Tasso, on the cliff over Marina Piccola. Five acres of citrus garden behind it and a private lift straight down to the water.

items.title: The citrus gardens, then the lift to the sea
items.detail: Unpack properly — this is home for five nights

items.title: Aperitivo on the terrace over the bay
items.detail: Vesuvius on the far shore, and it goes pink at sunset

items.title: Dinner — Terrazza Bosquet
items.detail: The hotel's Michelin-starred room, on the terrace. Worth booking for the first night rather than the last.

days.title: Sorrento, at walking pace
days.kicker: SORRENTO — the town, the lemon groves, and the first desk day
days.changeNote: New. Built around the work-from-home week — mornings are the trip, afternoons from about 2:30pm are held open for the desk.
days.note: Every coast day is shaped the same way: the outing happens in the morning and early afternoon, you're back at the hotel by 7pm at the latest, and dinner is at the hotel or a few minutes' walk from it. That holds for all five nights — the Ravello day on Sep 4 is the only one where it's tight. If you're working European hours rather than US ones, flip the desk block to the morning; nothing else has to move.

items.title: Breakfast in the garden
items.detail: Under the lemon and orange trees, which is the whole reason people book this hotel

items.title: Sorrento on foot
items.detail: Piazza Tasso, the shopfronts of Via San Cesareo, and the Vallone dei Mulini — a ruined mill at the bottom of a gorge, swallowed by ferns, right in the middle of town

items.title: I Giardini di Cataldo
items.detail: A working lemon and orange grove in the centre of Sorrento, free to walk through, with limoncello made on site at the end of it

items.title: Lunch at Marina Grande — Bagni Delfino
items.detail: A wooden deck out over the water in the old fishing village below town. Fritto misto and a carafe of white.

items.title: Desk hours
items.detail: Back up for the working afternoon. Fibre in the rooms, and the garden terrace is the quiet spot if the room feels small by day three.

items.title: Swim, or the pool on the cliff
items.detail: The private lift drops you at Marina Piccola if you want salt water instead

items.title: Dinner — O'Parrucchiano La Favorita
items.detail: Tables set among the lemon trees of a 19th-century greenhouse. Cannelloni was invented in this kitchen, so order it. Six minutes from the hotel door.

days.title: Capri, twenty-five minutes away
days.changeNote: Capri is now a short hop rather than an expedition — the crossing from Sorrento is 25 minutes against about 50 from Naples, which buys back most of a morning.
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan. Buy the return leg when you buy the outbound.

items.title: Down to Marina Piccola by the hotel lift
items.detail: The ferry pier is a two-minute walk from where the lift lets you out

items.title: Fast ferry — Sorrento → Capri
items.detail: About 25 minutes; up to forty crossings a day in high season, but they still sell out at the counter in August. Book online the night before.

items.title: Round-the-island boat from Marina Grande
items.detail: The Faraglioni, the grottoes and the swim coves — Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough to enter. Two hours or so.

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp, looking straight down at the Faraglioni

items.title: Ferry back to Sorrento
items.detail: Check the final sailing when you land in the morning — missing the last boat means a night on the island

items.title: Desk hours
items.detail: Back at the hotel with the US afternoon still ahead

items.title: Dinner — Il Buco
items.detail: Michelin-starred, in the wine cellar of an old monastery just off Piazza Tasso

days.title: Positano, for an afternoon
days.kicker: SORRENTO → POSITANO — by ferry, there and back
days.changeNote: New. Positano gets its own half-day by sea instead of being glimpsed from a passing ferry.
days.note: Positano has no real port, just a pier that closes in rough weather — check the morning update if the forecast looks unsettled. It is also almost entirely stairs; wear the right shoes.

items.title: Slow morning — swim and breakfast
items.detail: No ticket, no departure to make until mid-morning

items.title: Ferry to Positano
items.detail: About 35 minutes down the peninsula from Sorrento. Mid-April to mid-October only, and worth booking the day before in August.

items.title: Positano from the water, then from the stairs
items.detail: The pastel town stacked straight up from Spiaggia Grande, and the majolica dome of Santa Maria Assunta. The best picture is from the boat coming in — have the camera out before you dock.

items.title: Lunch — Chez Black, on the beach
items.detail: Right on Spiaggia Grande, unpretentious despite the address. La Tagliata up in the hills is the other option if you'd rather climb.

items.title: Via Pasitea and the boutiques
items.detail: Linen and sandals made to measure while you wait — Positano's actual local industry

items.title: Golden hour on the Villa Comunale terrace
items.detail: A public balcony on the cliff edge, three minutes from the hotel, straight out over the Bay of Naples. The light goes gold about an hour before the sun drops behind Ischia.

items.title: Dinner — Ristorante Museo Caruso
items.detail: A block off Piazza Tasso, walls covered in Caruso memorabilia, and the seafood is better than the theme suggests

days.title: Amalfi below, Ravello above
days.kicker: SORRENTO → AMALFI & RAVELLO — ferry down, driver up, driver home
days.changeNote: Amalfi and Ravello are now a single day trip from the Sorrento base rather than a two-night stay — which is what makes the five-night work week possible.
days.note: The longest day out of the five, and the one that has to be watched: leave Ravello by 5pm and you're back at the hotel around 6:30pm. The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5, so a concert in the Villa Rufolo gardens is available tonight — it's the one thing worth breaking the 7pm rule for, but it means a 1h30 drive back near midnight.

items.title: Ferry to Amalfi, via Positano
items.detail: About 40 minutes direct, a little over an hour with the Positano call. Seasonal — mid-April to mid-October.

items.title: Amalfi's Duomo and the Cloister of Paradise
items.detail: The striped façade of Sant'Andrea at the top of sixty-two steps, and a 13th-century cloister of interlaced Arab-Norman arches behind it

items.title: The lemon lanes behind the piazza
items.detail: Up the Valle dei Mulini path — Amalfi made paper here for six hundred years, and the ruined mills are still in the gorge

items.title: Lunch — Da Gemma
items.detail: Just off Piazza Duomo, a terrace above the street, and the best table in Amalfi town

items.title: Private driver up to Ravello
items.detail: Thirty minutes of switchbacks, a thousand feet straight up from the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity — a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea behind them

items.title: Villa Rufolo's gardens
items.detail: Wagner's Klingsor garden, and the festival stage cantilevered out over the drop

items.title: Driver back to Sorrento
items.detail: Over the pass rather than around the coast — about an hour and a half either way. Leaving Ravello at five puts you back at the hotel around 6:30pm.

items.title: Dinner — L'Antica Trattoria
items.detail: Under a pergola in the old town, and the last proper dinner on the coast

days.title: Back to Rome for the last night
days.kicker: SORRENTO → ROME — driver to Naples, then the Frecciarossa
days.changeNote: Rome's finale hotel is now the InterContinental Ambasciatori Palace, a few doors along Via Vittorio Veneto from where the Nobu was — same street, same five-minute walk to Villa Borghese.

items.title: Private driver to Napoli Centrale
items.detail: About 1h15 back around the bay

items.title: Frecciarossa to Rome
items.detail: Napoli Centrale → Roma Termini, direct — about 1h10, departures roughly every half hour

items.title: Arrive Roma Termini; taxi to the hotel
Check in — InterContinental Rome Ambasciatori Palace
items.detail: Via Vittorio Veneto, the La Dolce Vita address, at the Villa Borghese end of the street — five minutes from the gardens you photographed on the first Wednesday

items.title: Down Via Veneto to the Spanish Steps
items.detail: Past Palazzo Margherita and the Capuchin crypt, then down to Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Trevi Fountain, one last time
items.detail: Ten minutes on from the steps, and worth the crowd on a final evening

items.title: Aperitivo on Via Veneto
items.detail: The hotel's own bar, or Harry's Bar a few doors down

items.title: Farewell dinner — Aroma, at Palazzo Manfredi
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on a rooftop that looks straight into the Colosseum. Book this one early; there are only a dozen tables with the view.

items.title: Taxi to FCO
items.detail: About forty minutes on an empty Sunday road. No rental to return — that ended in Florence on Aug 31.

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

hotels.name: Hotel Trame
hotels.blurb: A former Franciscan monastery two streets from Campo de' Fiori. Confirmed.

hotels.name: W Florence
hotels.blurb: Piazza dell'Unità Italiana, two minutes from the Santa Maria Novella platforms and eight from the rental desks. Deluxe King, $563/night before taxes and fees.

hotels.name: Il Castelfalfi
hotels.blurb: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, with Tuscany's largest golf course and its own vineyards. Room Classic with balcony, $839/night before taxes and fees.

hotels.name: Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria
hotels.blurb: Not yet booked — the proposal for the five-night coast base. Piazza Tasso, on the cliff over Marina Piccola, with five acres of citrus garden and a private lift to the water. Ferries to Capri, Positano and Amalfi leave from the pier below.

hotels.name: InterContinental Rome Ambasciatori Palace
hotels.blurb: Via Vittorio Veneto, five minutes from Villa Borghese and Porta Pinciana. $457/night before taxes and fees.

drivers.note: Pre-booked NCC, name board at arrivals — book before you fly
Frecciarossa, roughly every half hour; the W is a two-minute walk from the platform

drivers.route: Borgo Ognissanti, Florence — outside the ZTL
drivers.note: Florence pickup, Florence drop-off, two days only — not FCO

drivers.route: Castelfalfi → San Gimignano → horseback tour → back
Il Castelfalfi → Borgo Ognissanti (drop the car) → Napoli Centrale
drivers.note: The rental ends where it started. Book the Florence–Naples Frecciarossa ahead — it's the longest leg of the trip.

drivers.route: Napoli Centrale → Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria, Sorrento
drivers.note: Pre-book. The Circumvesuviana is cheaper but has nowhere to put luggage in August.
Up to forty crossings a day in high season — still book online the night before, and note the last sailing back
Seasonal, mid-April to mid-October. Positano's pier closes in rough seas.

drivers.route: Sorrento → Amalfi by sea; Amalfi → Ravello → Sorrento by road
drivers.note: Ravello is car-free at the top — the driver waits at the gate. Allow 1h30 for the drive back over the pass.
No rental to return — that was dropped off in Florence on Aug 31

driversNote: Almost the whole trip is car-free: a private driver in from FCO, the Frecciarossa up to Florence, a two-day rental for Tuscany, then rail to Naples and a driver over the peninsula to Sorrento, where everything after is a ferry. The car is collected on Aug 29 on Borgo Ognissanti — just outside Florence's ZTL, eight minutes on foot from the W — and returned to the same desk on Aug 31 before the train south. Two driving days, not fourteen. The IDP ships by Aug 3; pack it with the physical licence even though it's only needed that once. Never drive into a historic centre — Florence's ZTL alone is ~€200 a crossing. Castelfalfi has its own parking, and the Excelsior Vittoria's garage is the only place in central Sorrento you'd want to park anyway. The Sorrento–Positano–Amalfi ferries run mid-April to mid-October, so the whole window is covered, but any of them can be cancelled for weather — keep the hotel's driver number as a backup for the Amalfi day.

bookings.item: Book the Sorrento hotel — five nights, Aug 31 → Sep 5
bookings.detail: The one open booking left, and the biggest single line in the budget. Holding the old lodging total leaves $6,906 for these five nights, or about $1,381 a night. The Excelsior Vittoria is penciled in at ~$1,150/night, which lands ~$1,150 under the ceiling. Whatever you pick, confirm the wifi is fibre and the room has a desk — one of you is working four of these five days.

bookings.item: Book the FCO → Hotel Trame private driver
bookings.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board — roughly €70–90 for the two of you, against a €55 flat-rate official taxi if you would rather just walk to the rank. Give them the ITA flight number so the driver tracks the landing.

bookings.item: Rebook the rental car — Florence pickup and drop-off, Aug 29 → Aug 31
bookings.detail: The old reservation is still FCO Aug 24 → FCO Sep 6. It needs to become Borgo Ognissanti, Florence, Aug 29 → Florence Aug 31: two days rather than fourteen, both ends the same city. Re-quote before cancelling — the old €1,087.81 figure was for a fourteen-day FCO round trip and will not carry over.

bookings.item: Horseback riding, lunch & winery tour — San Gimignano, Sun Aug 30
bookings.detail: San Gimignano Experience, 11am–3pm, ~€120pp: about an hour on horseback through vineyards and olive groves, then lunch, a cellar tour and wine tastings. Note the date moved from Sep 4 to Aug 30 in the replan. Meets at the Bivio Volterra bus stop — book ahead, it's a small-group tour.

bookings.item: Frecciarossa — Firenze S.M.N. → Napoli Centrale, Aug 31
bookings.detail: About 3 hours, direct via Rome. The longest single leg of the trip and the one where booking ahead actually saves money.

bookings.item: Private driver — Napoli Centrale → Sorrento, Aug 31, and back on Sep 5
bookings.detail: About 1h15 each way. Book both directions with the same operator. The Circumvesuviana costs €5 but has no luggage space and no air conditioning worth the name in August.

bookings.item: Timed entries — Accademia (Aug 27), Duomo dome + Uffizi (Aug 28)
bookings.detail: Only two Florence days now, so these three are the tight ones. Book the dome climb first — it has the fewest slots of anything in the city — then the Uffizi guided slot behind it.

bookings.item: Vatican early entry (Aug 25), Colosseum arena floor (Aug 26)
bookings.detail: Both need booking — the Vatican slots go first.

bookings.item: Florence opera — La Traviata at St. Mark's, Aug 28
bookings.detail: Moved from Sep 2 in the replan. Now on the single full Florence day, after the Boboli afternoon.

bookings.item: Rome opera — All Saints' Anglican, Aug 25
bookings.detail: Confirm the programme is posted before booking.

bookings.item: Frecciarossa — Napoli Centrale → Roma Termini, Sep 5
bookings.detail: About 1h10, departures every half hour — no scarcity, book for the fare.

bookings.item: Capri ferry — Sorrento → Capri return, Sep 2
bookings.detail: About 25 minutes each way from Marina Piccola, directly below the hotel lift. Book both legs online the night before and note the last sailing back. The round-the-island boat can be picked up at Capri's Marina Grande on the day.

Both from Sorrento's Marina Piccola, seasonal but well inside the window. Two or three morning departures down the coast and two or three back in the afternoon — check the current timetable close to the date, the schedules shift with the season.
Picks you up in Amalfi after lunch, waits at Ravello's gate (the town is car-free), and drives you back over the pass. Roughly 2 hours of driving in total.

bookings.item: Ravello Festival — check the Sep 4 programme
bookings.detail: The festival runs to Sep 5, so your Ravello day is inside the window. A concert on the Villa Rufolo stage is the one thing worth reshaping the evening for — but it means a 1h30 drive back to Sorrento afterwards.

Borgo San Jacopo Aug 27 · Sostanza Aug 28 · La Via del Sale Aug 29 & 30 · Terrazza Bosquet Aug 31 · O'Parrucchiano Sep 1 · Il Buco Sep 2 · Da Gemma (lunch) Sep 4 · Aroma at Palazzo Manfredi Sep 5. Aroma and Terrazza Bosquet are the two to book first.

bookingsRuledOut.reason: No open night in the schedule for a Verona detour — every night from Aug 24 to Sep 5 has a hotel booked elsewhere.
Dropped in the replan. Naples is now a change of trains on the way down and on the way back — the five nights it would have cost go to the single coast base instead.

bookingsRuledOut.item: Volterra, and a second Tuscan wine estate
bookingsRuledOut.reason: Tuscany is two nights. San Gimignano and the horseback vineyard tour fill the one full day there.

bookingsRuledOut.item: Positano or Amalfi as the base
bookingsRuledOut.reason: Both are beautiful and both are stairs. With one of you working four days out of five, Sorrento wins on flat ground, a real town, fibre, and ferries to everywhere else on the coast.

budget.note: 5 hotels, 13 nights. Confirmed or quoted: Trame ($1,588), W Florence ($1,236), Castelfalfi ($1,841), InterContinental Ambasciatori ($527). The Sorrento base is the one line still open — penciled in at $5,750 for five nights, against a ceiling of $6,906 if you hold the old $12,098 lodging total.

Estimate. FCO private driver, Rome→Florence train, a 2-day Florence–Tuscany rental car, Florence→Naples train, Naples↔Sorrento private drivers both ways, ferries to Capri, Positano and Amalfi, the Amalfi→Ravello→Sorrento driver, and Naples→Rome train.

Vatican, Colosseum, Florence galleries and the dome climb, two operas, the Capri round-the-island boat, Villa Cimbrone and Villa Rufolo, and the San Gimignano horseback/lunch/winery tour (~€120pp, ~$260 for two).
